raw_response:
My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for three generations. I have about 10 mu of contracted land, flat and good for crops. I never went to school — everything I know I learned watching my father and talking with neighbors. I don't think about it too much. Everyone here grows winter wheat then summer corn on the same fields. That's what this land is for. That's what the market takes. That's what I know.

For wheat, I'll plough in early October like always, work in some base fertilizer — diammonium phosphate and urea together — then plant. I buy the improved seed from the county seed shop in Quzhou town, same variety my neighbor uses, around 25 yuan a jin. I won't plant less than last year. Come spring I'll pump water four times from the village canal — before sowing, before it freezes, once in March when it greens up, and once around grain filling. My father always said wheat needs water or it gives you nothing. I'll spray twice, once for rust and once for aphids in May.

After wheat harvest in June I'll turn the stubble under with the rotary machine I share with my brother-in-law, then plant hybrid corn seed. Corn is easier — summer rain helps and I only need to pump once or twice if it's dry. I'll top-dress urea twice. Spray once for corn borer. Harvest end of September.

I won't try anything new this year. New things cost money and risk.
